llms.body:
# Knock

> Knock is agentic customer engagement infrastructure to grow faster. Ship cross-channel lifecycle and transactional messaging from your favorite agent.

"Your agent" is Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or another client you connect to Knock. "Agent steps" run inside Knock workflows. "The Knock agent" works in the Knock dashboard.

## Start with an agent
- [Connect your agent to Knock](https://knock.app/features/agents): Set up Knock from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or Codex.
- MCP server: https://mcp.knock.app/mcp
- [MCP server card](https://knock.app/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json): Machine-readable description of the Knock MCP server.
- CLI: `npm install -g @knocklabs/cli`
- [Skills](https://github.com/knocklabs/skills): Open-source skills that teach AI coding agents to work with Knock. Install with `npx skills add knocklabs/skills`.
- [Docs for agents](https://docs.knock.app/llms.txt): Index of every docs page as Markdown.
- [Full docs](https://docs.knock.app/llms-full.txt): All docs in one file.

## Pricing
- [Pricing](https://knock.app/pricing): The Free plan includes 10K messages per month. The Starter plan starts at $250 per month and includes 50K messages, then $.005 per message. Enterprise has volume-based pricing through sales.

## Product
- [Workflows](https://knock.app/features/workflows): Orchestrate your entire customer journey. A single workflow engine for powering transactional and lifecycle messaging across every channel.
- [Guides](https://knock.app/features/guides): In-app messaging with your own components. Ship paywalls, dialogs, and nudges powered by your components. Enable non-engineers to edit copy and targeting in Knock.
- [Broadcasts](https://knock.app/features/broadcasts): Intelligent, multi-channel announcements. Send one-time announcements across every channel, with complete control over audience, content, and delivery.
- [Data activation](https://knock.app/features/data-activation): Unify and activate your data. Ingest from your product and warehouse, build audiences, and trigger relevant messaging.
- [Observability](https://knock.app/features/observability): See every workflow run, message, and log across channels.
- [Template management](https://knock.app/features/template-management): Manage templates, layouts, partials, and translations in one place, with version control.
- [Preferences](https://knock.app/features/preferences): Enable recipients to choose which messages they get and on which channels.

## Channels
- [In-app](https://knock.app/channels/in-app-notifications): Ship real-time, in-app notifications in a day.
- [SlackKit](https://knock.app/channels/slackkit): Send customer notifications through Slack, Teams, and Discord with chat integrations and component libraries.
- [Email](https://knock.app/channels/email): Send transactional, marketing, and product emails with multi-channel workflows, a dynamic template editor, and global brand styles.
- [Push](https://knock.app/channels/push): Create push notification experiences for iOS and Android apps with pre-built integrations, SDKs, APIs, and embeddable UIs.
- [SMS](https://knock.app/channels/sms): Send event-driven, transactional, and promotional SMS messages with APIs, a visual workflow editor, and deliverability tooling.
- [Integrations](https://knock.app/integrations): Every channel and provider Knock connects to, including chat on Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, and WhatsApp.

## Solutions
- [Engineering](https://knock.app/solutions/engineering): Messaging infrastructure that scales with you. Use Knock's APIs to engage users, run workflows, and manage user preferences.
- [Growth + product](https://knock.app/solutions/growth-product): Accelerate growth with timely, personalized messaging across any channel. Activate data, target users, and trigger automated workflows that convert.
- [Marketing operations](https://knock.app/solutions/marketing-operations): Unify your data from any source to enable personalized messaging at scale.

## Developers
- [Documentation](https://docs.knock.app): Learn key concepts and integrate Knock
- [Knock CLI](https://knock.app/cli): Bring Knock to your terminal
- [Quick start](https://docs.knock.app/getting-started/quick-start/general): Send your first notification with Knock
- [Tutorials](https://docs.knock.app/tutorials/alerting): How to power common use cases
- [SDKs](https://docs.knock.app/developer-tools/sdks): Libraries and tools for interacting with your Knock integration.
- [API reference](https://docs.knock.app/api-reference/overview)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/knocklabs)

- [Top 9 React notification libraries in 2026](https://knock.app/blog/the-top-notification-libraries-for-react): In this article, we'll explore the nine best open-source notification libraries for React applications in 2026, categorized by their primary use cases and strengths.
- [The developer's guide to notification system tooling in 2026](https://knock.app/blog/guide-to-notification-systems-and-tooling): An in-depth look at notification systems and the ecosystem of tools, frameworks, and vendors available.
- [Twilio Notify EOL: Migrating to Knock](https://knock.app/blog/migrating-from-twilio-notify-to-knock): How to transition your Twilio Notify implementation to Knock
- [How to add an in-app notification feed to Next.js](https://knock.app/blog/how-to-add-an-in-app-notification-feed-to-nextjs-15): A high level tutorial on how to get started with Knock's drop-in notification feed components and Next.js
- [Troubleshooting channel_not_found in Slack incoming webhooks](https://knock.app/blog/troubleshooting-channel-not-found-in-slack-incoming-webhooks): Learn how to resolve the channel_not_found error when using Slack's Incoming Webhooks to send messages to different channels.
- [How we think about writing for robots with llms.txt](https://knock.app/blog/how-we-think-about-writing-for-robots-with-llms-txt): A deep dive into how we built our llms.txt file for our docs.
- [Building effective component libraries: a startup perspective on design systems](https://knock.app/blog/building-effective-component-libraries): How we approach building and maintaining our component library at Knock

### Manuals

#### Notification infrastructure

- [Introduction to notification infrastructure](https://knock.app/manuals/notification-infrastructure/introduction-to-notification-infrastructure): The typical path that leads companies to need a more comprehensive solution for notifications, and the benefits that notification infrastructure platforms provide.
- [Understanding notification channels](https://knock.app/manuals/notification-infrastructure/understanding-notification-channels): Why cross-channel support matters, and why you want to avoid setting up and managing notifications across different channels by yourself.
- [How to choose a notification infrastructure platform](https://knock.app/manuals/notification-infrastructure/how-to-choose-a-notification-infrastructure-platform): Learn when you might need a more comprehensive notification solution, what criteria to look for, and how to choose the right notification platform for your product.

#### Transactional email

- [Introduction to transactional email](https://knock.app/manuals/transactional-email/introduction-to-transactional-email): Learn what "transactional" means, see real-world examples of transactional emails, and understand why deliverability is critical for this type of communication.
- [How to build a transactional email system](https://knock.app/manuals/transactional-email/how-to-build-a-transactional-email-system): This chapter discusses how to approach building your own transactional email infrastructure (spoiler: don't), how to choose the right email service provider, and how to set up authentication for your email domains with SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and BIMI.
- [Best practices for sending transactional email](https://knock.app/manuals/transactional-email/best-practices-for-sending-transactional-email): This chapter covers best practices for managing email deliverability and discusses how localization, template management, and personalization issues can be solved with notification infrastructure. 
- [How to measure transactional email performance](https://knock.app/manuals/transactional-email/how-to-measure-transactional-email-performance): This chapter addresses all of the different metrics you should monitor to make sure your transactional emails are sending successfully over time, including things like delivery rate, bounce rate, time to inbox, and more.

#### Push notifications

- [Introduction to push notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/push-notifications/introduction-to-push-notifications): Learn what push notifications are, how they work, and real-world examples of effective push notifications.
- [Core components of a push notification system](https://knock.app/manuals/push-notifications/core-components-of-push-notification-systems): This chapter explains the fundamental building blocks required to send your first push notification, including token management, provider authentication, payload structure, and the sending pipeline.
- [The technical implementation of push notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/push-notifications/technical-implementation-of-push-notifications): This chapter explains the critical technical components and architectural decisions that will enable you to scale billions of push notifications sending to millions of users reliably.
- [Building a robust preference system](https://knock.app/manuals/push-notifications/building-a-preference-system): How to navigate the complexity of push notification preferences, with a focus on how your application’s preference logic interacts with the device’s native controls that users rely on to manage their experience.
- [Deciding how to deliver your push notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/push-notifications/delivering-push-notifications): This chapter will help you decide whether or not to build your own infrastructure (spoiler: don't) and how to choose the right push notification provider.

#### SMS notifications

- [Introduction to SMS notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/sms-notifications/introduction-to-sms-notifications): Learn what SMS notifications are, how transactional and promotional SMS differ, how SMS delivery works, and the top use cases for SMS notifications, from authentication codes to shipping updates.
- [How to build an SMS notification system](https://knock.app/manuals/sms-notifications/how-to-build-an-sms-notification-system): The building blocks required to send your first SMS notification, including sending identities, rate limits, location-specific considerations, user preference management, and more.
- [Best practices for sending SMS notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/sms-notifications/best-practices-for-sending-sms-notifications): Best practices for sending your first SMS notification, including tips for writing effective, well-formatted content that drives action and strategies to reduce your costs when sending at scale.
- [How to choose an SMS provider](https://knock.app/manuals/sms-notifications/how-to-choose-an-sms-notification-system): Learn how to evaluate SMS providers on pricing, developer experience, and advanced features, and compare the top SMS providers, including Twilio, Amazon SNS, Sinch, and Vonage.

#### In-app messaging

- [Introduction to in-app messaging](https://knock.app/manuals/in-app-messaging/introduction-to-in-app-messaging): Learn what in-app messaging is, what it takes to use it well, and real-world use cases and examples of effective in-app messages.
- [How to build an in-app messaging system](https://knock.app/manuals/in-app-messaging/how-to-build-in-app-messaging-system): Learn how in-app messaging works, including the backend architecture, real-time delivery infrastructure, storage and state management, UI components, and more.
- [Best practices for in-app messaging](https://knock.app/manuals/in-app-messaging/best-practices-for-in-app-messaging): Best practices for sending your first in-app message, including tips for choosing the right format, writing actionable content, targeting the right users, and more.
- [How to choose an in-app messaging solution](https://knock.app/manuals/in-app-messaging/how-to-choose-an-in-app-messaging-solution): Learn how to choose the right in-app messaging solution, considering flexibility and customization, performance and reliability, developer experience, cost structure, and more.

#### Slack notifications

- [Introduction to Slack notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/slack-notifications/introduction-to-slack-notifications): Learn what Slack notifications are, why they matter for modern product experiences, and real-world examples of teams using Slack to deliver timely, contextual updates to users.
- [How to send Slack notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/slack-notifications/how-to-send-slack-notifications): The technical details of how Slack notifications work under the hood. Learn how to authenticate and send messages through the Slack API, handle delivery logic, manage message state, and build a robust backend workflow that ensures every message reaches the right destination.
- [Best practices for sending Slack notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/slack-notifications/best-practices-for-slack-notifications): Once you’re set up to send notifications, this chapter helps you optimize them for impact. We’ll walk through best practices for message design, formatting, interactivity, and targeting, so your Slack messages feel useful, not noisy.
- [Deciding how to deliver your Slack notifications](https://knock.app/manuals/slack-notifications/delivering-slack-notifications): The choice between building your own Slack notification system and using a managed service is one of the most critical decisions you'll make. Let's examine when each approach makes sense.

#### Liquid templating language

- [An introduction to Liquid](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/introduction-to-liquid): In this chapter, you'll learn what Liquid is, how it works, and get introduced to Liquid's three core components through real-world examples.
- [Understanding Liquid keys](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/understanding-liquid-keys): Learn how Liquid keys work, including how to access simple and nested data, work with arrays by index, and apply best practices for defensive templating.
- [Understanding Liquid operators](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/understanding-liquid-operators): Learn how Liquid operators define how values are compared and combined, including the rules for truthy and falsy values, comparison operators, and logical operators that form the foundation for conditional expressions.
- [Understanding Liquid filters](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/understanding-liquid-filters): In this chapter, you'll learn how to use Liquid filters to modify strings, numbers, arrays, and dates efficiently, turning raw input into precisely formatted output through filter chaining and transformations.
- [Understanding Liquid tags](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/understanding-liquid-tags): Learn how Liquid tags enable control flow, iteration, and variable assignment, so you can build dynamic, data-driven templates with loops, conditions, and logic that respond to different inputs.
- [Advanced Liquid concepts](https://knock.app/manuals/liquid-templating-language/advanced-liquid-concepts): In this final chapter, we'll go beyond the basics with advanced concepts like date and time handling, whitespace control, and data encoding to power sophisticated dynamic personalization inside Knock.

#### Effective product messaging

- [The product leader's guide to effective messaging](https://knock.app/manuals/product-leaders-guide-to-effective-notifications/the-product-leaders-guide-to-effective-notifications): Learn how to build an effective product notification strategy using behavioral data, event-based triggers, cross-channel orchestration, batching, personalization, and user preferences.

Agentic customer engagement to grow faster

Ship lifecycle and transactional messaging from your favorite agent. Start with a prompt, scale to millions of customers.

Case study

Case study

Orchestrate beautiful, cross-channel messaging

Coordinate in-app and out-of-app flows that reach the right users at the right moments. Send dynamic, on-brand messages across email, in-app, push, SMS, and chat.

The New user onboarding workflow in the builder, at Collab.io. An agent step is dragged in from Add a step under the new-user-signup trigger and its prompt is typed: Claude Sonnet 5 writes a welcome line for the recipient that fits their role, into a welcome_line response property. The welcome email greets the recipient by first name, then uses that line. After a 3 day delay, a branch on Created a project? sends a Day 3 tips email to people who have not created one yet and an in-app feed message to everyone else.

Trigger smart automations that send messages across any channel.

email / in-app / push / SMS / chat

Launch messaging flows with a prompt

Pick your agent and a use case, then use the prompt to build it.

Explore agents

Your agent

Use case

Your prompt

Prompt

Build an onboarding journey for new signups using Knock. Based on what we're building, create a welcome email on day 0, show an in-app guide on first login, and send a tips email on day 3 if they have not created a project.

Build in Knock
mcpdocs.knock.app/ai/mcp-servercli

All starter prompts, for people and agents

Connect your agent to the Knock MCP server at https://mcp.knock.app/mcp, or install the Knock CLI with npm install -g @knocklabs/cli. Then use any prompt below.

  • Knock: Build in Knock
  • Claude: First make sure to install the Knock connector.
  • ChatGPT: First make sure to install the Knock plugin.
  • Cursor: First make sure to install the Knock plugin.
  • Grok: First make sure to install the Knock plugin.
  • Slack: First make sure to connect Knock in Slack.
  • MCP: First make sure to connect the Knock MCP server.
  • CLI: First make sure to install the Knock CLI.

Onboarding (Lifecycle)

Build an onboarding journey for new signups using [Knock](https://knock.app). Based on what we're building, create a welcome email on day 0, show an in-app guide on first login, and send a tips email on day 3 if they have not created a project.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Trial ending (Lifecycle)

When a trial has 3 days left. Based on what we're building, create an email and show an in-app banner with an upgrade button using [Knock](https://knock.app). Stop as soon as the account upgrades.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Win-back (Lifecycle)

Find users with no activity in the last 30 days. Based on what we're building, create a win-back sequence using [Knock](https://knock.app) across email and push. Stop the sequence as soon as a user comes back.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

NPS survey (Lifecycle)

Based on what we're building, create an NPS survey using [Knock](https://knock.app) that shows in-app 30 days after signup. If a user does not answer within 3 days, send it by email.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Mentions (Transactional)

When someone is mentioned in a comment. Based on what we're building, create an in-app feed message using [Knock](https://knock.app) right away. If it is still unread after an hour, send one email per thread.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Feature launch (Promotional)

Based on what we're building, create a broadcast using [Knock](https://knock.app) that announces our new reporting feature to all workspace admins, with a matching in-app banner for one week. Use our default email layout.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Weekly digest (Product)

Based on what we're building, create a weekly digest workflow using [Knock](https://knock.app) that uses an agent step to summarize each user's activity from the past week, then sends it by email every Monday.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Usage limit (Product)

When an account reaches 80% of its plan limit. Based on what we're building, create an email and an in-app notification using [Knock](https://knock.app) for its admins, and again at 100%.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Failed payment (Transactional)

When a payment fails. Based on what we're building, create an email using [Knock](https://knock.app) for the billing contact right away and show an in-app alert to account admins until the payment succeeds.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Re-engagement (Lifecycle)

If a user has not logged in for 14 days. Based on what we're building, create an email using [Knock](https://knock.app), then a push on day 21.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Churn risk (Lifecycle)

When an account's weekly active users drop 50%. Based on what we're building, create a workflow using [Knock](https://knock.app) that sends an internal Slack alert to the CSM and a check-in email to the account owner.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Sync warehouse data (Setup)

Connect my Snowflake warehouse as a source using [Knock](https://knock.app). Based on what we're building, create a model querying the `users` table, then map the `email`, `name`, and `plan` columns to the matching user fields. Set the sync to run every hour.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Migration (Setup)

Read the templates and journeys in our current messaging tool. Based on what we're building, create workflows, templates, and layouts using [Knock](https://knock.app). List anything you could not migrate.

  • Open in Claude
  • Open in ChatGPT
  • Open in Cursor
  • Open in Grok

Unlock customer engagement that runs itself

Knock agents build journeys, analyze performance, and suggest improvements to meet your goals. You decide what ships.

Build

Set your goals, and Knock agents identify, build, and ship the customer journeys to hit them.

Run

Run agent steps in your workflows to enrich signups, summarize activity, and personalize messaging.

Improve

Knock agents find ways to increase activation, conversion, and retention. Each change waits on a branch for your review.

Unify product, CDP, and warehouse data

Sync data and events from your product, CDP, warehouse, and connected tools to build dynamic audiences and trigger messaging based on any attribute or signal.

Explore data activationBrowse integrations

Product usage from the Knock SDKs, traits from a CDP such as PostHog, Segment, or Amplitude, account data synced by Hightouch from a warehouse such as Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery, and billing data from Stripe flow into one user model in Knock as user properties.

A dynamic audience updates as those properties change, and a user entering the audience triggers a workflow.

Built for visibility and control

Agents work on branches, away from your live messaging. You read every change before you merge and publish it.

Explore observability

An agent's branch forks off main in coral. A person merges it and publishes it, and the change turns ink and goes live, where every run is logged and any version can be reverted.

  1. Work on a branch

    Agents work in isolation, not on your live messaging.

  2. Merge and publish

    A person reads the diff, then merges and publishes it.

  3. Monitor every run

    Logs show details for every step of every run.

  4. Analyze performance

    Measure the impact of your messaging across channels.

  5. Manage from your repo

    Merge and promote from the Knock CLI and CI/CD.

Knock delivers hundreds of millions of messages per month.

Dedicated success

Our team helps you plan, build, and launch your messaging.

Security is standard with support for SSO, RBAC, and SCIM.
